column3: Close to the Hebrew; “knowledge of wind” is rendered “empty knowledge.”
Close to the Hebrew; שִׂיחָה (“meditation, complaint”) is rendered “prayer.”
Close to the Hebrew; יִּרְזְמוּן (“flash”) is rendered “wink at.”
Close to the Hebrew; “holy ones” is rendered “His saints,” and NKJV supplies “God.”
Close to the Hebrew; “stored up for” is rendered “hidden from.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he is watched for the sword” is rendered “a sword is waiting for him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “with a neck” is rendered “stubbornly.”
NKJV capitalizes “His mouth,” taking it as God’s breath; the Hebrew “his mouth” is ambiguous.
